_about: Image tests (tools/images.py): each scene is drawn with midgard_runtime and these arguments plus --screenshot, then compared with <name>.png in this folder, or, with 'same_as', exactly with this run's image of an earlier scene. A scene may set its own tolerance (0-255 per colour channel) and max_bad (the fraction of pixels allowed past it).

scenes.name: bright
scenes._about: The demo scene three times brighter: highlights roll off towards white instead of clipping (tone mapping).

scenes.name: far_50km
scenes._about: The demo scene 50 km from the world's origin: camera-relative rendering makes it look exactly like the demo at the origin.

scenes.name: far_10000km
scenes._about: 10,000 km out, where a float steps by a metre: still the same picture.

scenes.name: materials
scenes._about: Spheres from smooth to rough (left to right) and plain to metal (top to bottom).

scenes.name: textures
scenes._about: One object per material texture: base colour, normal map, metal/roughness, occlusion, emissive. Its textures are magnified on screen, which drivers filter alike; near the spheres' edges they shrink, where drivers may choose mip levels differently, so up to 1% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: compressed
scenes._about: The textures scene with every texture through KTX2 (Basis UASTC) and the GPU's compressed format (BC7 here; RGBA where a GPU reads none). The same allowance as textures.

scenes.name: surfaces
scenes._about: Surface shaders (5.17): left to right the plain material, blue gloss stripes (six: their colour and count are the draw's settings), a dissolve (holes cut by noise with glowing edges), ripples (bent normals, a faint blue glow) and a shader the renderer doesn't have, drawn bright magenta. Noise is computed on the GPU, where drivers may round differently, so up to 1% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: lights
scenes._about: A red point light and a blue spot light in a dim scene.

scenes.name: shadows
scenes._about: Sun shadows on flat ground, from 2 to 45 metres away (all four cascades), and a plank's shadow apart from it. Drivers filter shadow edges a little differently, so up to 1% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: shadows_curved
scenes._about: Sun shadows on a small planet where 'up' leans 50 degrees from y: the cascades are built in the local up frame. The same allowance as shadows.

scenes.name: sky_day
scenes._about: The analytic sky by day (sun 35 degrees up, behind the camera) over a wide plain, with a thin haze that hides the farthest pillar in the sky's own colour.

scenes.name: sky_sunset
scenes._about: The sun 3 degrees up, ahead: its disc and glow, a warm horizon under a dark sky, long shadows, and fog lying low over the plain (thinning upwards).

scenes.name: shadows_phone
scenes._about: The shadows scene at the phone quality tier: two smaller cascades over 30 m, so the farther pillars cast none, and harder shadow edges.

scenes.name: sky_sunset_phone
scenes._about: The sunset at the phone quality tier: the same sky and fog, shorter and harder shadows.

scenes.name: sky_cloudy
scenes._about: The sky_day scene under broken cloud (milestone 5.15): white clouds drifting across the blue, thinning to the horizon, the sun still shining.

scenes.name: sky_storm
scenes._about: The sky_day scene in a storm: overcast and dark grey, the light dimmed and tinted blue-grey, fog closing in to 400 m so the far pillars fade, the shadows faint.

scenes.name: sky_rain
scenes._about: Rain (milestone 5.15 step 5): streaks blown sideways by the wind across a grey, cloudy day, fading out near the camera and with distance. Thin streaks rasterise a little differently between drivers: up to 3% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: sky_snow
scenes._about: Snow drifting down under an overcast sky: soft white flakes, larger near the camera. The same allowance as sky_rain.

scenes.name: sky_wet
scenes._about: After the rain (milestone 5.15 step 6): the ground soaked, darker, with the low sun's glare shining on it, the ball wet and glossy, under a clearing sky.

scenes.name: sky_snowed
scenes._about: After a snowfall: snow settled on what faces up (the ground, the top of the ball, the tops of the pillars), not on the pillars' sides.

scenes.name: colliders
scenes._about: Collider outlines (--debug-physics) over the scene: static scenery grey-green, a dynamic crate and ball orange, a kinematic capsule blue, a trigger yellow, a static convex rock grey-green with its faces' diagonals, and the player's capsule cyan. Lines are thin, so drivers draw their pixels a little differently: up to 2% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: skinned
scenes._about: GPU skinning (milestone 5.13): three tubes skinned to a three-joint chain, at rest, bent 60 degrees sideways and bent 90 degrees towards the camera (posed through the animation library), with their shadows skinned too. Shadow edges differ a little between drivers: up to 1% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: terrain_area
scenes._about: Streamed terrain on a bounded area, seen from above: hills from deterministic noise, finer near the camera, sinking to the ocean band at the map's edge, with water over the sea and the lakes (milestone 5.9).

scenes.name: terrain_strip
scenes._about: A flat-wrap cylinder's terrain rising to its end wall (the fortification look).

scenes.name: terrain_habitat
scenes._about: Inside a habitat: the ground curving up on both sides into the far side overhead, softened by the inside-world haze, with the barrier closing its far end.

scenes.name: terrain_habitat_ground
scenes._about: Standing on a habitat's floor, looking ahead: the ground round the player lit like the rest (the far side overhead casts no shadow on it; it used to darken a disc round the camera as far as shadows reach).

scenes.name: terrain_habitat_rod
scenes._about: Standing on a habitat's floor looking up: the light rod down its axis (5 m across, glowing as bright as the day there), the far side beyond it in the haze. The rod lights the ground straight down everywhere.

scenes.name: terrain_hollow_light
scenes._about: Inside a 1 km hollow world looking up: the light sphere at the centre (10 m across), small and bright in the haze's glow round it, the far side's seas beyond.

scenes.name: terrain_planet_biomes
scenes._about: A 3 km planet with a climate and four biomes, from 5 km up (milestone 5.11): tan desert and savanna round the equator, green forest between, grey tundra towards the pole and ice where it is below freezing; the seas dark beneath. Up comes from the world's shape in the shader.

scenes.name: terrain_placed
scenes._about: A world type's objects placed over a bounded area (milestone 5.11): trees (a trunk and a crown) on the gentle ground, grey boulders leaning with the steeper, each at its own turn and size, with their shadows.

scenes.name: terrain_snowfall
scenes._about: terrain_placed after a snowfall (milestone 5.15 step 6): settled snow over the hills, patchy where it thins, on the tops of the boulders and the trees' crowns, not on the steepest rock.

scenes.name: space
scenes._about: System space (milestone 5.16): the 3 km planet of terrain_planet_biomes from 6 km over its ground, whole against a black sky of stars from its seed (some brighter, some warmer or bluer). Single-pixel stars are drawn a little differently between drivers: up to 3% of pixels may differ.

scenes.name: terrain_shore
scenes._about: Low over the sea by a coast (milestone 5.9): water from the Earth-like environment's look, its waves reflecting the sky, the island beyond, and the shallows below showing the ground through foam.

scenes.name: terrain_winter
scenes._about: terrain_area in deep winter: snow down to just above the beaches, the sea and lakes as before (milestone 5.9's terrain material).

scenes.name: terrain_autumn
scenes._about: terrain_area in autumn: the grass turned golden-brown, more where the ground is lush.

scenes.name: terrain_planet
scenes._about: A 3 km planet from low orbit over a cube corner, where three of the cube-sphere's faces meet: hills, lakes and seas run across the face edges with no seams (milestone 5.10).

scenes.name: terrain_planet_low
scenes._about: Low over the planet's ground by the edge between two faces, looking across it: one surface, lit the same either side.

scenes.name: terrain_hollow
scenes._about: Inside a 2.5 km hollow world by a face edge: the ground and seas curving up all round into the far side, softened by the inside-world haze (scaled to its size); its water's waves come from 3D, so they too run on across face edges.

scenes.name: terrain_hollow_far
scenes._about: Inside an 8 km hollow world, looking up at its far side 16 km away: drawn in a few coarse chunks, its seas and coasts showing faintly through the inside-world haze, which thins with the world's size (1.2 / radius per metre) so the far side always shows (milestone 5.10).
scenes._tolerance: Its lakes 16 km away are a pixel or less across, where drivers round differently: 1.3% of pixels differed on lavapipe (CI run 41317155990), so 3% may.

scenes.name: ui_desktop
scenes._about: The UI test screen (milestone 6.0) over the demo scene at a desktop size: RmlUi's text (Inconsolata), buttons, check box, slider, text field and a scrolling list, blended over the scene. Before the picture, the runtime's screen checks pass: a gamepad reaches every control and no text overflows.

scenes.name: ui_phone
scenes._about: The same screen at a phone's size and scale (1.5 pixels a dp) with a pretend notch (90 pixels) and gesture bar (60) kept clear; its checks include a finger's: every control at least 44 dp and inside the safe area.
